friendship-and-social-problems.task: During actual cooperative play practise giving/receiving a relevant encouraging message, taking turns, inviting another child and sustaining a reciprocal shared activity. Use original fictional disputes over one shared tool or different building ideas: describe the problem, hear both views, propose a safe fair solution and try it, then review whether it worked. A child can decline touch/play or seek adult help; friendship is not compulsory agreement with a peer. Use a real shared build with enough accessible roles and one shared tool: each partner contributes an idea, listens and completes an agreed part. Compare including, honesty, reliability and kindness with bossing/excluding. Reflect on an actual helpful choice without awarding a permanent good-friend label; a positive message must be relevant to its recipient, not a forced compliment.
friendship-and-social-problems.positive: Actual reciprocal communication, turn-taking, relationship-maintaining choices and problem-solving are separately evidenced across accessible play.
friendship-and-social-problems.nearMiss: Repeats a compliment script without listening, solves a dispute by exclusion/coercion, or calls adult-imposed compliance the child’s own negotiated solution.
friendship-and-social-problems.transfer: Change partner, shared resource or disagreement and adapt the strategy.
friendship-and-social-problems.limits: No forced physical affection, smile, eye-contact norm or demand to be friends with an unsafe person.

responsibility-regulation-and-learning.task: Across supported ordinary routines, child selects a meaningful manageable responsibility, tries an accessible unfamiliar task, starts a chosen step and seeks appropriate help. When a plan fails or setting changes, identify a feeling/need, choose a strategy such as pausing, asking or changing the plan and try again. In a supplied peer story, notice a feeling clue, ask rather than assume, and choose an empathetic response respecting the peer’s preference. Compare quiet-work and shared-play expectations with reasons. Record context/support over time instead of converting one moment into a permanent motivation/confidence trait. In actual routines, the learner selects a responsibility and states a first step, tries it and reviews the result with recorded support. Offer two genuine choices and compare consequences before deciding. Practise two available settling strategies; do not induce distress to test independent use. The original changed task is a paper bridge whose first span bends: choose help, another fold or a smaller load, test the change and explain what was learned. Compare a quiet-book context with shared construction and explain a suitable change in conduct. Initiative/willingness/confidence remain contextual observations, not a binary personality score.
responsibility-regulation-and-learning.positive: Agency, responsibility, strategy use, adaptation and an appropriate empathetic response are supported through observable choices.
responsibility-regulation-and-learning.nearMiss: Adult completes every choice; silent compliance or cheerful appearance is scored as confidence; or a child is penalised for valid distress or asking for help.
responsibility-regulation-and-learning.transfer: Changed routine/task/peer cue requires a different available strategy.
responsibility-regulation-and-learning.dispositionBoundary: Willingness, confidence, positive self-image and self-regulation are contextual developmental aims; do not infer stable character/mastery or demand one emotional display.

health-food-hygiene-and-feelings.task: Use the attributed health-source account and original fictional active/rest scenarios to explain possible mind/body effects without an exercise test, fitness norm or treatment claim. Use accurate varied-food picture cards and the actual HealthCanada food-guide snapshot to plan an illustrative varied meal/snack including vegetables/fruit,wholegrains,protein and water, explaining simple benefits and a feasible access/preparation strategy; no real eating or household income disclosure is required. Actually practise supported soap-and-water handwashing (wet,soap,rub including fingers/thumbs,rinse,dry) with the public-health20second adult timing support, and discuss relevant times such as before food/after toilet or coughing. Through play or a fictional character, discuss happy/unhappy experiences and reasons; private autobiography and happiness are not scored as correctness. Use a real drinking-water/rest opportunity without withholding any basic need; exercise participation is not required. Include a fictional tired character to explain the role of rest and sleep. For hygiene, also discuss adult-supported tooth care and practise an elbow/tissue cough action without spraying or spreading materials; tooth brushing is not independently certified by the handwashing station. Use the supplied seven-day routine record honestly: record actual opportunity/support, an optional chosen action and reflection; never fill invented successes. Provide a fresh fictional feeling story so passing on private details does not prevent discussing reasons for happiness or unhappiness.
health-food-hygiene-and-feelings.positive: Effects/benefits are discussed, a feasible varied-food choice is explained, hygiene is actually practised, and feelings are described with contextual reasons.
health-food-hygiene-and-feelings.nearMiss: Makes a body-size/moral-worth judgment, recites foods while shaming unavailable food, demonstrates only pretend handwashing without the actual practice duty, or demands that every child feel happy after movement.
health-food-hygiene-and-feelings.transfer: New suitable food/routine/fictional feeling context requires an adapted explanation.
health-food-hygiene-and-feelings.limits: Adult follows allergies,access,actual safe-use and available clean-water arrangements. No supplements, restrictive diet, calorie calculation, diagnosis or clinical exercise prescription.

safety-and-get-help.task: Before the actual build/movement activities identify a safe work area and applicable classroom rules, demonstrate safe handling, and explain what injury a chosen rule helps prevent. Use an original fictional card: a pupil has a collision and says their head hurts or they do not feel right. Choose to stop the activity and tell a trusted adult for help; no child diagnoses a concussion or decides return-to-play. Separately use offline fictional in-person/online discomfort cards (a person asks for an address or a game feels unsafe): pause/stop, avoid sharing private information and seek a suitable trusted adult. Change the setting and identify another help route if the first adult is unavailable.
safety-and-get-help.positive: Actual safe practice, a reason for the rule and age-appropriate help-seeking in both in-person/online cases are demonstrated.
safety-and-get-help.nearMiss: Recites a rule while handling equipment unsafely, keeps playing through a suspected injury, or shares personal information to make an unfamiliar online person happy.
safety-and-get-help.transfer: Different activity/contact context requires a suitable safe action and help route.
safety-and-get-help.limits: Fictional scenarios only; no actual injury demonstration, clinical assessment, recovery timetable, compulsory trauma disclosure or real stranger contact.

fine-motor-and-cooperative-play.task: Use actual tabletop construction, drawing and art with adult-approved card, blunt scissors, joining tools and accessible materials. Make a small model by fitting, placing, cutting, folding and joining pieces, checking position and fit against the intended design. Offer an ordinary manageable construction challenge; the pupil may change method, ask for help, pause or retry without manufacturing distress. In an actual non-physical cooperative building or board game, agree roles and turns, explain a strategy, try it and adapt to a changed shared resource. Keep the actual small-movement and spatial decisions identifiable; adult completion or a diagram alone is insufficient. No travelling route, ball skill, balance station, warm-up, fitness test or daily exercise participation is required.
fine-motor-and-cooperative-play.positive: Actual fine-motor control, spatial fit, supported persistence and cooperative strategies are checked separately; no gross-motor result is inferred.
fine-motor-and-cooperative-play.nearMiss: A group product certifies each member, an adult does the fine movements, or a fine-motor success is used to certify the excluded whole-body duty.
fine-motor-and-cooperative-play.transfer: Change piece size, joining tool, shared resource or partner; adapt the actual fine-motor or cooperative strategy.
fine-motor-and-cooperative-play.resourceCondition: Actual accessible supervised materials and benign cooperative activity are required. No Physical Education schedule or performance condition.

seven-day-routine-record.instructions: Choose a feasible health/safety routine with the learner, record actual opportunities and support for seven days, review an obstacle and an adjustment, and identify a suitable way to help another person. Blank fields are intentional, not completed observations.

food-and-feelings-cards.task: Use accurate adult-selected food pictures with the linked applicable guide. Create an illustrative varied meal or snack, explain a supported benefit and one feasible access/preparation idea. This is not a complete nutrient-function or day-menu assessment.
feelingStories: A character is pleased when a friend joins a chosen building game.
A character feels unhappy when a tower falls; another wants a quiet break rather than rebuilding.
The same noisy game feels exciting to one character and uncomfortable to another.
questions: What happened, what feeling is supported and what remains uncertain?
What could the character ask or choose next?
Could another person feel differently, and why?

conditions.wholeClaims: Source tasks contribute components; broader inherited mastery inventories and hard prerequisite readiness remain separate. No definitions or learner state changed.
conditions.contextualAims: Willingness, initiative, self-confidence, persistence and emotional regulation are contextual developmental aims. Record opportunities/choices/support; never infer enduring character or demand happy/calm appearance.
conditions.participation: Actual benign cooperative play, fine-motor practice and health routines are retained. Physical Education participation and gross-motor assessment are excluded.
conditions.safety: Provide accessible supervised choices and appropriate actual materials. No forced disclosure, real unsafe contact or clinical diagnosis.
conditions.coverageMeaning: Full is prepared source-task authoring with named components, not observed attainment or universal developmental milestones.
